scope: Thirty distinct source and enforcement audit questions; this is not a claim of thirty discovered defects or complete static coverage.
baseline_note: Current origin/main when the audit branch was integrated; the requested pending suppression-hardening PR started at 2addb305.
fixes: Resolve class, comprehension, annotation, decorator and default evaluation scopes for proven indirect typing.cast access.
Respect generic type parameters and closer real bindings without confusing valid shadowing with native typing.cast.
Reject Ruff-honored scoped Flake8 file suppressions.
Reject source analyzeUnannotatedFunctions=false and disableBytesTypePromotions=false controls that remove native type diagnostics.

passes.question: Can inline/file/range/blanket comments, consumer Ruff config, exclusions, or existing baselines waive the required direct-cast ban?
passes.finding: Packaged ignore-noqa policy remains required, non-baselineable, and cannot be rule-excluded; other API exceptions still work. Explicit whole-path/capability scope boundaries remain intentional.

passes.question: Are absolute typing/typing_extensions wildcard imports detected without treating relative or lookalike modules as native typing?
passes.finding: Both native wildcard forms are detected; relative/lookalike imports abstain; protected evidence supersedes duplicate generic syntax findings.

passes.question: Does literal-key proof fold only bounded side-effect-free text while preserving dynamic and non-cast keys?
passes.finding: Literal additions, adjacent strings and static f-strings are recognized. Variable keys, interpolated strings, unknown syntax and oversized/deep text are intentionally not evaluated.

passes.question: Do getattr fallback, module dict, vars, and __getattribute__ carriers preserve API identity without guessing keyword expansions?
passes.finding: All four supported carriers are enforced; opaque keyword expansions abstain. Native failure and protected-finding metadata remain tested.

passes.question: Does builtin shadowing distinguish an actual builtin call from a function parameter or unrelated lexical binding?
passes.finding: Parameter shadowing abstains; a same-named parameter in an unrelated function does not hide a proven module-level access. Class-local builtin shadowing is corrected under pass 7.

passes.question: Does receiver proof stop after rebinding, member mutation, escape, or unbounded namespace access?
passes.finding: Existing conservative identity contracts remain unchanged. This helper does not claim to prove arbitrary mutable/reflected/dynamic programs.

passes.question: Does lexical resolution separate class bodies from nested code and evaluate defaults, decorators, and lazy annotations in their native scopes?
passes.finding: Corrected class lexical capture plus enclosing evaluation scopes for defaults, decorators, function annotations, and generic parameter bounds/defaults. Class body locals are visible only where Python makes them visible; method return annotations and generic owner bounds/defaults preserve outer class annotation scope. Explicit function/class body imports can override an enclosing generic parameter.

passes.question: Are lambda/comprehension bodies distinct from the first iterable evaluation scope, including class-local sources?
passes.finding: Nested lambda/comprehension bodies do not capture class locals; a comprehension first iterable still evaluates in its enclosing class scope. Existing stable module-level lambda access remains enforced.

passes.question: Do NFKC identifiers, string-literal spelling, CRLF/non-BMP regions, and UTF-8 BOM coordinates remain correct?
passes.finding: Identifier normalization recognizes equivalent Python names without normalizing runtime string literals. Existing coordinate tests and all 93 native-prefilter cases pass.

passes.question: Can PEP 695 type parameters shadow a typing module or builtin and manufacture a false native-cast proof?
passes.finding: Four original type-parameter shadowing false positives are fixed. Visible TypeVar/TypeVarTuple/ParamSpec names block native proof, while closer local imports win in body scope, owner defaults/decorators use outer scope, and bounds/defaults exclude owner body locals. Twenty independent review cases now match native runtime and expected detector results.

passes.question: Can bare, empty, malformed or partial Sarj selectors waive a diagnostic?
passes.finding: Only the complete named selector grammar suppresses; case-insensitive exact comma lists and supported single-dash reasons remain valid.

passes.question: Do Pyright directives distinguish actual file configuration from malformed syntax and nested prose?
passes.finding: Explicit enableTypeIgnoreComments=false keeps the nested candidate ineffective. The initial strict-only probe was a false lead caused by a leading type:ignore, already owned by required PGH003. No nested-directive change was made.

passes.question: Can supported boolean file controls remove actual type errors without SARJ523?
passes.finding: Ruff/BasedPyright source controls remain unchanged; SARJ523 now rejects the two proven false settings. analyzeUnannotatedFunctions removes the body operator error but still reports unknown return type and exits1; bytes promotion changes exit1 to0.
passes.fix: Extend the existing named disabled-check set by analyzeUnannotatedFunctions and disableBytesTypePromotions; do not infer weakening from arbitrary boolean names.

passes.question: Can named Flake8 file-noqa bypass the exact local suppression boundary while inline/prose forms remain inert?
passes.finding: Ruff0.17 honors Flake8 F401 and TID251 file selectors. F401 still leaves TID251 active and vice versa, so this is scoped file suppression, not a claim that codes are ignored. Named standalone forms now emit one SARJ523; inert inline/prose forms do not.
passes.fix: Recognize standalone named flake8:noqa file directives separately so Ruff banned-api precedence cannot exempt this previously unowned form.

passes.question: Are missing and closed generic reasons rejected without overrejecting a concrete boundary explanation?
passes.finding: SARJ419 remains a bounded lexical generic-phrase check; it cannot prove a human explanation true or sufficient. No speculative expansion was justified.

passes.question: Can a second directive or issue-number hash hide an explicit generic reason or cause duplicate diagnostics?
passes.finding: Shared trailing concrete explanations remain supported; an explicit generic reason on either directive still reports exactly once; #123 remains reason content.

passes.question: Can string, docstring, f-string or line-ending representation change whether a marker is a real Python comment?
passes.finding: Tokenized comment provenance excludes data while preserving real comments with BOM/CRLF.

passes.question: Does an exact local waiver remain bounded across sibling rules, sibling functions, and shadowed process receivers?
passes.finding: Scope and alias analysis stay with the owning source rule; suppression parsing does not infer behavior from variable names.

passes.question: Can parse, size or read failures make selected Python analysis report clean?
passes.finding: All three existing report-contract cases pass: FAILED/INCONCLUSIVE, exit2 and analyzer-failure. Per-rule abstention is not conflated with complete source analysis.

passes.question: Can a source integrity rule waive itself, including case variants, rule exclusion or a diagnostic baseline?
passes.finding: Protected native policy findings remain nonbaselineable and required despite global/scoped rule exclusions; explicit whole-path and partial-check boundaries remain documented and are covered by the 21-test adjacent suite. Package suites run separately because their conftest modules share a tests.conftest name.

passes.question: Can source directives disable the suppression validators themselves?
Can consumer ESLint configuration omit mandatory source rules?
Can native bulk suppressions waive full mandatory findings while partial scopes remain partial?
Can manifest rule exclusions, scoped overrides or baselines remove mandatory findings?
Are disabled capabilities and explicit partial checks reported as deliberate boundaries?
Do parser, configuration and missing-engine failures fail closed?
Can native ignore configuration or sibling paths silently lose selected-file coverage?
passes.finding: The original audit's pass result did not exercise checkout ancestors. A separate follow-up reproduced production diagnostics disappearing beneath exempt-named ancestors and scopes shared test/generated/script/story gates to the explicit ESLint cwd, preserving physical filenames and per-project ownership caching.

passes.question: Does the mandatory floor cover all eight selected JS/TS extensions and hidden source?
Are explained exact local exceptions, directive-like strings and concrete prose preserved?
passes.finding: Original exact local exception, string, and prose coverage is unchanged. Separate follow-up controls preserve actual in-project exemptions, generated basenames/source markers, and import-binding boundaries after ancestor normalization.

passes.question: Do merge/dedup, warning staging and console exits preserve mandatory error severity?

validation.python: 3.15.0; native cast scope fixtures additionally execute on 3.14.7
commands: uv --directory packages/python run pytest -q tests/test_cast_access.py tests/test_native_symbol_prefilters.py
validation.full_gate: Final qualification is recorded in the pull request after execution.

path_follow_up.scope: Separate follow-up; original audit still contains thirty questions, not thirty discovered defects.
path_follow_up.qualification: Final qualification is recorded in the follow-up pull request after execution.

corpus.scope: Identical captured bytes of 898 already-local tracked Python files; helper-only analysis, with seeded/runtime cases providing positive evidence.
corpus.limitation: Same-process timing under concurrent verification; no full-engine performance or speedup claim.

limitations: Unknown or mutable module identity, arbitrary aliasing, opaque keys, and dynamic namespace mutation retain conservative abstention.
Explicit whole-path exclusions, disabled capabilities, and deliberately selected partial checks remain analysis boundaries.
The native cast ban and mandatory suppression floor cannot be waived by a source comment or diagnostic baseline within their selected scope.
Other legitimate exact local API exceptions keep their documented boundary contracts; this does not ban every explained SDK import.
No autofix, consumer rule waiver, baseline increase or new lint suppression was added by these follow-up fixes.
